events.title: Emperor Caracalla is murdered near Carrhae
events.description: Caracalla was stabbed to death by a soldier while travelling to a temple near Carrhae in Mesopotamia. His praetorian prefect Macrinus, who had arranged the killing, became the first emperor not of senatorial rank.
events.html: Caracalla was stabbed to death by a soldier while travelling to a temple near Carrhae in Mesopotamia. His praetorian prefect Macrinus, who had arranged the killing, became the first emperor not of senatorial rank.

events.title: The Abbasids defeat Ya'qub ibn al-Layth at Dayr al-Aqul
events.description: On the Tigris south-east of Baghdad, the Abbasid regent al-Muwaffaq defeated the Saffarid ruler Ya'qub ibn al-Layth, who was marching on Baghdad, after flooding the ground before his army. Ya'qub abandoned his attempt to take Iraq and withdrew to Khuzistan.

events.title: New Norman cathedral at Winchester is consecrated
events.description: Bishop Walkelin's Romanesque cathedral at Winchester was consecrated in the presence of bishops and abbots. Later extended, it is now the longest medieval cathedral in Europe.
events.html: Bishop Walkelin's Romanesque cathedral at Winchester was consecrated in the presence of bishops and abbots. Later extended, it is now the longest medieval cathedral in Europe.

events.title: Farmer unearths the Venus de Milo on Milos
events.description: A peasant named Yorgos Kentrotas found the marble statue in the ruins of ancient Milos. Bought by the French and taken to the Louvre, the armless Aphrodite became one of the most famous sculptures in the world.
events.html: A peasant named Yorgos Kentrotas found the marble statue in the ruins of ancient Milos. Bought by the French and taken to the Louvre, the armless Aphrodite became one of the most famous sculptures in the world.

events.title: Britain and France sign the Entente Cordiale
events.description: A set of agreements settled colonial disputes, with Britain recognised in Egypt and France in Morocco. The understanding ended centuries of rivalry and drew the two powers together before 1914.
events.html: A set of agreements settled colonial disputes, with Britain recognised in Egypt and France in Morocco. The understanding ended centuries of rivalry and drew the two powers together before 1914.

events.title: Seventeenth Amendment introduces direct election of US senators
events.description: Connecticut's ratification completed the Seventeenth Amendment, transferring the choice of senators from state legislatures to voters. Secretary of State Bryan certified it at the end of May.
events.html: Connecticut's ratification completed the Seventeenth Amendment, transferring the choice of senators from state legislatures to voters. Secretary of State Bryan certified it at the end of May.

events.title: Jomo Kenyatta is convicted at the Kapenguria trial
events.description: A colonial court in Kenya sentenced Jomo Kenyatta and five others to seven years' hard labour for allegedly managing Mau Mau. The widely criticised verdict made him a national symbol; he became Kenya's first president.

events.title: Pablo Picasso dies at Mougins aged 91
events.description: Pablo Picasso died at his home in the south of France. Co-founder of Cubism and creator of Guernica, he had reshaped modern art over a career lasting more than seventy years.
events.html: Pablo Picasso died at his home in the south of France. Co-founder of Cubism and creator of Guernica, he had reshaped modern art over a career lasting more than seventy years.
